facts: Start the second emulator on its own port, for example with -port 5556, so it is emulator-5556.
With two devices ready, a call must name one: --device emulator-5556, or a client's device option; with none named, Mobium refuses, listing the ready devices.

To drive both at once, give each run its own daemon with MOBIUM_SESSION (a client's session option): one daemon holds a call for its whole length, and an emulator's 15 map calls took 22.3s sharing a daemon against 0.3s on its own.
note: 'Running two at once' answers the start; 'Parallel runs', which retrieval ranked first, answers running them side by side, so ADD it. Fact 2 reworded: SETUP lists MOBIUM_SESSION as an alternative to --device, but the code does not pick a device by session (internal/device/adb.go:424-430 refuses with two ready; agent/backend.go:394 reuses a session only once it is open on one device).

findings.what: 'Then pass --device emulator-5556 to every command, or run each one under its own MOBIUM_SESSION, or give a client the device option' offers MOBIUM_SESSION as a way to pick the emulator. It names a daemon, not a device: a fresh session's first call with two emulators ready and no --device is refused; only after a session is open on one device do its later calls follow it. Read from code, not run.
findings.evidence: internal/device/adb.go:424-430 '%d devices are ready (%s) — pick one with --device <serial>'; internal/agent/backend.go:385-399 openSessionFor reuses the single open session when no serial is given
